newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty gains in thin trade, depo liquidity edges up.
newsitem.headline: Zloty gains in thin trade, depo liquidity edges up.

text.p: The Polish zloty firmed on Tuesday as a light currency selling trend continued despite a slight improvement in the money market's liquidity, but turnover was cut in half to roughly $200 million, dealers said.

They said that the currency-selling sentiment may remain intact on Wednesday if hard currencies continue to flood the market as foreign firms and banks operating in Poland increased capital before the end of December.
"Trade was slow today but a light currency selling trend remained as foreign banks and firms increase capital before the end of the year," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale.
The zloty closed at 2.89/2.82 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than yesterday's close at 2.78/2.72 percent.
It was at 2.8595/10 to the dollar, down from 2.8580/90 on Monday and at 1.8392/10 to the mark, up from 1.8416/25.
Last week banks cut currency positions mainly to boost liquidity on the severly squeezed money market with one-day rates trading at the 25 percent lombard rate.

Dealers said zloty trade was thin as there were only minute orders from domestic or foreign clients. They said the zloty's upward drive on Tuesday was also supported by the dollar's dip against the mark in European trade.

One-day deposit rates fell as the system regained some liquidity and pushed overnight rates down to 21.50/24.90 percent, down from opening's 24.80/24.90 percent. Tomorrow/next depos were at 22.50/24.00 percent, down from 24.80/24.95.

Dealers said liquidity may improve further on Wednesday on the back of inflows from maturing T-bills which may support falling trend in deposit rates. The finance ministry is to buy-back a net 735 million zlotys worth of T-bills tomorrow.
The National Bank of Poland set December's reserve money target band between 34.43 and 35.13 billion zlotys from November's band between 33.29 and 33.99 billion zlotys.
